craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of proclamation — the hammer now proclaims: breath demoted → rest unfolds → Māyā named → mother proclaimed → fence → double-held VERDICT. Question + nominal verdict; close kept verbless per L3 note (SA akhyāter jīvatā param). Rejected: (a) adding verbs to close → killed: verblessness is the verdict-form. (b) settling sādhitā scope → killed: held open per BOUNDARY. Read aloud: HOW-could-BREATH ev-er-PROVE … PAST non-SHOW-ing.

lines: How could breath ever prove its hold on that self-nature?
In recognition — by living-ness, past non-showing.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tadātmanaiva tasya syāt kathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā sādhitā pratyabhijñāyām akhyāter jīvatā param
notes: line 2 nominal, mirroring verbless SA close (akhyāter jīvatā param)

reads_against.argmap: Can breath restrain that self-nature? → Breath-restraint is unprovable; living-ness outlies non-showing — recognition, not breath, settles it.
c1_essence: Breath, body, and the eightfold city are demoted to knowables: no ordering lies in breath, no restraint touches the self, and living-ness stands beyond non-showing (vv19-22).

Rest unfolds into freedom, doership, lordship; Māyā named from power alone; the beginningless mother-principle proclaimed; pervasion fenced to I-sharers; the world verdict that-nondual-made (vv23-27).
